newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares inch higher, seen hemmed in.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares inch higher, seen hemmed in.

text.p: Austrian shares inched higher on Thursday after trading in a slim range for most of the day, and traders said the market was holding its breath before Friday's expiry of futures and options.

Market participants agreed the ATX index had room to move about 20 points higher at the start of next week once the expiry had been digested. "There's some really good support at 1,290 points in any case," said one.
The ATX index of 21 shares rose 2.49 points or 0.19 percent to close at 1,299.96. Among its constituents, 15 gainers outweighed five losers, one issue closed unchanged.
Steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm led the day's winners, rising 2.1 percent or 19 schillings to 935.
Elsewhere, Creditanstalt preferred firmed seven schillings to 500 after reports the bank had raised operating profit in the first five months by more than 29 percent.
Bank Austria, which acquired control of Creditanstalt earlier this year, was up one schilling at 395.
The day's decliners were led by hosiery maker Wolford, down 2.09 percent or 25 schillings at 1,169.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX futures for June delivery rose 4.7 points to 1,296.7 on turnover of 1,270 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
